prompts.text: What's something you'd like to become a little better at by this time next year?
Tell me about a skill you learnt slowly and eventually started enjoying.
Choose one ambitious new hobby or build on a skill you already use?
You get a free class in any practical subject for six months. What would you learn?
A long-term goal can begin as curiosity about one very small thing.
You don't need a dramatic transformation for a year to feel worthwhile.
Which small achievement would make your future self quietly proud?
Recall a goal you began without realising how important it would become.
An opportunity to practise a new skill appears in your neighbourhood. What would make you sign up?
Set a clear milestone for next year or choose a direction and leave room to explore?
Which part of your daily routine would you most like to simplify?
Describe a time a small improvement freed up energy for something enjoyable.
Have more free time in the mornings or a calmer end to your evenings?
You can redesign one ordinary weekday without changing your work responsibilities. What would move first?
The future people hope for often includes fewer inconveniences, not just bigger achievements.
A sustainable routine is more valuable than a perfect schedule that lasts one week.
What ordinary task would you be happy to spend less time doing in five years?
Recall a period when your routine changed and you discovered a better way to organise your day.
Your ideal weekday includes an unexpected hour of free time. How would you like to use it?
A steadier weekly rhythm or more flexibility to choose each day as it comes?
What's a place you'd love to visit because you're curious about daily life there?
Tell me about a destination that became interesting after somebody described it personally.
Spend a month getting to know one city or take several short trips to different places?
You can stay in an unfamiliar town for a week and follow local routines. What would you want to try?
Travel ambitions can be about understanding a place rather than collecting landmarks.
A nearby destination can be as rewarding as an expensive overseas trip.
Which journey would you like to take at a more relaxed pace someday?
Recall discovering that your favourite part of a trip wasn't on the original itinerary.
You can plan one thoughtful future outing with a close friend. What would make it meaningful?
Visit a place connected to your family's history or somewhere entirely unfamiliar?
What kind of home environment do you imagine enjoying a decade from now?
Describe staying somewhere that helped you realise what you value in a living space.
A small, easy-to-maintain home near activity or a quieter place with more room?
You have to sketch one corner of an ideal future home. What would you put there?
A comfortable home is often defined by how people spend their time in it.
A future living plan should reflect real habits rather than only impressive photographs.
What's one feature of your current space you'd want to keep wherever you live next?
Recall a home you visited where one ordinary detail made it welcoming.
You can design a shared courtyard for a future neighbourhood. What activity should it support?
A bright space for hosting a few friends or a private corner for reading and thinking?
Which kind of community project would you like to see succeed in your area?
Tell me about watching a small local initiative grow through consistent effort.
Help create a neighbourhood reading room or improve a local walking space?
Your community receives a modest grant to improve daily life. What would you ask residents before proposing ideas?
Shared improvements often begin with people noticing the same small problem.
A useful community goal doesn't need to be the most visible project in town.
What practical change would make your neighbourhood more welcoming to newcomers?
Recall someone who quietly contributed to a place you cared about.
You have one weekend to help launch a small volunteer project. What would make it manageable?
Support a short, clearly defined local project or a routine that people can maintain together?
What's a creative project you hope to try before worrying whether you're good at it?
Describe having an idea you put aside because you didn't know where to begin.
Spend a month experimenting with a new art form or finish something you've already started?
You get access to a creative studio for a day with no expectation of producing a finished piece. What would you explore?
Some ambitions begin as things people enjoy imagining rather than targets they must immediately reach.
It can be worthwhile to pursue a creative idea that never becomes a business.
What would you make if the result didn't have to impress anybody?
Recall discovering a surprising interest through somebody else's creative project.
An old project notebook turns up in five years. What would you hope to see you've followed through on?
Keep a portfolio of little experiments or work patiently towards one larger piece?
What's a relationship or friendship habit you'd like to practise more consistently?
Tell me about changing how you keep in touch with someone and finding it easier for both of you.
Make more time for familiar friends or get to know people outside your usual circle?
Your future schedule becomes busier. Which kind of social commitment would you want to protect?
Future plans are often easier to sustain when they account for other people's lives too.
A good social goal may be about being more present rather than meeting more people.
What would a well-balanced social week look like for you?
Recall a friendship that grew because somebody made a simple recurring effort.
You'd like to establish an inexpensive monthly gathering. What would make it welcoming and easy to maintain?
Plan a regular coffee with one friend or host a small rotating group activity?
What have you begun caring less about as your priorities have changed?
Describe a goal that sounded attractive until you learnt what it would demand day to day.
Spend more energy improving a familiar strength or exploring whether an old ambition still suits you?
A future opportunity looks impressive but leaves little room for things you enjoy. What would you want to clarify?
Not every abandoned plan represents a failure; sometimes the underlying priorities change.
Changing direction after learning more can be a sign of sound judgement.
Which expectation about adulthood do you now see differently?
Recall learning that somebody you admired had chosen an unexpected path.
You can ask a version of yourself ten years older one question about priorities. What would it be?
Keep a long-term goal unchanged or revisit it every year to see if it still fits?
What's one topic you'd like to understand better as the world changes?
Tell me about learning a useful new technology later than most people around you.
Become more confident with practical digital tools or learn a hands-on craft that technology can't replace?
Your local library offers free workshops about everyday technology. What should the first session cover?
People often learn new tools most easily when the tools solve a familiar problem.
The best future technology is often the kind that requires less attention from people.
What everyday invention would you like to see made easier to repair?
Recall a new tool that seemed confusing until someone explained it simply.
You can improve one public service through better design rather than adding new features. What would you choose?
Learn how an emerging tool works or focus on understanding the privacy choices around it?
What would you like people close to you to remember about the way you spent your time?
Describe an ordinary moment that helped you realise what makes a day satisfying.
Build a tradition that lasts for years or create many small shared experiences along the way?
You write a short note to open in ten years. Which everyday detail would you include so it feels real?
A meaningful future can be measured by recurring moments rather than a single major achievement.
Some of the best life ambitions don't fit neatly on a résumé.
Which quality would you like to become known for through your everyday actions?
Recall seeing somebody live in a way that made you rethink what success meant.
Someone asks you to describe your ideal future without mentioning possessions or job titles. What would you say?
A life with steady familiar rituals or one with room for frequent new discoveries?
